turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict each
candidate's largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, then select the 5
candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20 pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
To predict the largest Second Harmonic Generation (SHG) tensor component $|d_{ij}|$ for the candidate materials and find the ones closest to 20 pm/V, we must evaluate their crystal structures, constituent elements, and band gaps. The SHG response in non-centrosymmetric crystals is highly dependent on the polarizability of the bonds (e.g., chalcogenides and pnictides yield higher SHG than oxides/halides) and is inversely proportional to the band gap ($E_g$). 

Here is the step-by-step reasoning for the most relevant candidates:

1. **c083 ($\text{Li}_4\text{As}_4\text{S}_8 \rightarrow \text{LiAsS}_2$)**: 
   Alkali metal thioarsenates are well-known infrared NLO materials. $\text{LiAsS}_2$ features highly polarizable $\text{AsS}_3$ lone-pair stereochemically active polyhedra. Its experimental SHG response is widely reported to be approximately $1.5 \times \text{AgGaS}_2$ (where $\text{AgGaS}_2$ has $d_{36} \approx 13.5$ pm/V). This yields a $|d_{ij}|$ of **~20 pm/V**, making it a perfect match.

2. **c071 ($\text{Al}_2\text{Cu}_2\text{Ge}_2\text{Se}_8 \rightarrow \text{CuAlGeSe}_4$)**: 
   This is a quaternary diamond-like chalcogenide. It is structurally and chemically analogous to the well-known $\text{Cu}_2\text{ZnGeSe}_4$ ($d_{36} \approx 22$ pm/V). The substitution of Zn with Al slightly widens the band gap, which marginally reduces the nonlinear optical response, bringing its $|d_{ij}|$ to **~20 pm/V**.

3. **c021 ($\text{Al}_2\text{Ga}_2\text{Cu}_4\text{Se}_4\text{S}_4 \rightarrow \text{Cu}_2\text{AlGaS}_2\text{Se}_2$)**: 
   This is a solid solution of chalcopyrite materials. The SHG coefficients of the parent end-members are: $\text{CuAlSe}_2$ (~23 pm/V), $\text{CuGaSe}_2$ (~28 pm/V), $\text{CuAlS}_2$ (~10 pm/V), and $\text{CuGaS}_2$ (~11 pm/V). The mixed-anion/mixed-cation composition averages these polarizabilities out, yielding an estimated $|d_{ij}|$ of **~18–19 pm/V**.

4. **c027 ($\text{Si}_4\text{C}_4 \rightarrow \text{3C-SiC}$)**: 
   The dataset contains several SiC polytypes (c024–c029). Candidate c027 corresponds to the cubic zincblende phase (3C-SiC, $a \approx 4.378$ Å). While hexagonal polytypes (like 6H-SiC) have $d_{33} \approx 11-12$ pm/V, the 3C-SiC polytype has a well-established $d_{36}$ of **~18 pm/V**.

5. **c093 ($\text{Al}_4\text{Cu}_4\text{Se}_8 \rightarrow \text{CuAlSe}_2$)**: 
   This is a standard ternary chalcopyrite NLO material. Its experimental $d_{36}$ tensor component is well-documented in literature to be **~23 pm/V**. 

*(Note: Other materials in the pool either have much lower SHG (e.g., chlorides/bromides like c053, c086 are $<5$ pm/V; wide-gap sulfides like c081 $\text{ZnAl}_2\text{S}_4$ are $\sim 10$ pm/V) or much higher SHG (e.g., c030 $\text{CdSiP}_2$ is $\sim 84$ pm/V; c079 $\text{Ba}_4\text{Ge}_2\text{Te}_5\text{Se}_3$ is $>40$ pm/V).)*

Final: c083, c071, c021, c027, c093
